verifiedSources.verifiedBy: curl HTTP 200, 245,304 bytes; `file` confirms valid 30-page PDF v1.4; opened and read the full text. IMPORTANT FINDING (this session, verified against the primary text, not a news snippet): the Act creates a 'SARAL Keralam' statutory authority for investment projects with capital investment EXCEEDING RS. 25 CRORE, with its 'SARAL Secretariat' being KSIDC (state level) / District Industries Centre (district level) — but the Act's own Schedule (Annexure, see sections 7 & 11) lists only 7 specific laws it overrides: the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act 1994, Kerala Municipality Act 1994, Kerala Cinemas Regulation Act 1958, Kerala Panchayat/Municipality Building Rules 2019, and the Kerala Panchayat/Municipality 'Issue of Licence to Enterprises' Rules 2025/2026. The Factories Act, 1948 / Kerala Factories Rules 1957 is NOT among the scheduled laws, so on the verified primary text, SARAL Keralam does NOT currently supersede or replace the Factory License (FAL) process or K-SWIFT's factories-licensing function — it targets local-body (panchayat/municipality) trade/building licences for large investment projects. The schedule can be amended later by government notification (clause 23), so this could change, but as enacted it does not confirm the news-reported 'K-SWIFT replacement for factory licensing' theory

remarks: THIS RETRY SUBSTANTIALLY IMPROVED ON THE PRIOR RESULT: verifiedSources grew from 2 to 11 (a 5.5x increase). The key unlock was discovering that fabkerala.gov.in's https:// endpoint still resets this session's proxy connection on every attempt ('Recv failure: Connection reset by peer', unchanged from the prior attempt), but its plain http:// endpoint works and serves the exact same real department content — home page, FAQ, user-guides/downloads page, and all four previously-excluded PDFs (Kerala Factories Rules 1957, two 2025 Gazette notifications, and the 2025 RTS Gazette notification) all now verified over http. This fixed 6 of the 18 prior exclusions outright.

kswift.kerala.gov.in (the actual K-SWIFT filing portal) and idms.fabkerala.gov.in (the FABOS application/login system) remain genuinely unreachable this session on BOTH http and https, across repeated attempts each (connection reset on https, operation-timed-out-with-zero-bytes on http) — this is a different, more severe failure mode than the https-only TLS reset affecting fabkerala.gov.in's own content pages, and is consistent with (though does not prove) these specific application subdomains being degraded, deprecated, or migrating.

Acting on this task's explicit instruction to verify the 'SARAL Kerala' transition lead: found and verified the actual SARAL Keralam Bill, 2026 (Bill No. 19) full text via the Kerala Niyamasabha's own published-bills page (niyamasabha.org) — a genuine .gov-adjacent legislative-secretariat source, not a news snippet. HOWEVER, reading the verified primary text shows the news framing ('SARAL to replace K-SWIFT for factory licensing') is NOT borne out by the Act's own Schedule: SARAL Keralam's statutory override currently applies only to 7 named local-body laws (Panchayat Raj Act, Municipality Act, Cinemas Regulation Act, building rules, and 'Issue of Licence to Enterprises' rules) for investment projects over Rs. 25 crore — the Factories Act, 1948 and Kerala Factories Rules, 1957 are NOT in that schedule. So this verified document corrects, rather than confirms, the unconfirmed news lead: as enacted, SARAL Keralam is a parallel/overlapping single-window mechanism for large investment projects' LOCAL BODY clearances, not a replacement for the Factories & Boilers department's own Factory License (FAL) process or for K-SWIFT's role in it. (The schedule is notification-amendable per clause 23, so this could change in the future.)

The proxy's broader Indian-gov.in connectivity issues appear unchanged in kind from the prior attempt: the live proxy status log at the time of this retry still showed fresh ws_closed_mid_exchange failures for OTHER states' factory/industries portals (e.g. sewasetu.assam.gov.in, industries.cg.gov.in, ciflabour.assam.gov.in, rajfab.rajasthan.gov.in) within the same minute, confirming this is a persistent network-wide condition, not something that resolved generally — the improvement here came specifically from trying the http:// (non-TLS) variant of fabkerala.gov.in, which happened to route around the TLS-level reset for that particular host.
